name: losing
quote: Where, oh where, has my little dog gone?
description: Sadness caused by something you had valued being taken from you without anything to show for it.

variations.name: losing a game or contest
variations.description: Most of the time we play a game or enter a contest there's a hope we'll win. We regret the disappearance of hope and whatever resources of time and money were invested. For important contests like an election, we may have anxiety about the consequences of the loss.

variations.name: losing an important contest you were favored to win
variations.description: If you or your team were the predicted winner, the loss may may affect perceived social status and incur shame, rationalization, self-doubt, or even grief.

variations.name: losing a loved one
variations.description: If a person, group, or creature important to you dies or otherwise disappears, it may leave a void of grief. Depending on the manner of the disappearance, it may also cause resentment or anger.

variations.name: losing an important asset
variations.description: If something special like a job, a ring, money, or a house is lost, destroyed, or stolen, it may cause grief, frustration, fear, or other negative experiences.

variations.name: losing social status
variations.description: If the loss comes with a perceived downgrade in social status, it's likely to cause any number of negative experiences.

variations.name: losing something considered neutral or negative
variations.description: Phrases like 'losing weight' and 'losing inhibition' are just double negatives -- these can be interpreted to mean 'gaining fitness' and 'finding courage'.

commentaries.quote: It is better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.
It's not whether you win or lose, but how you play the game.

conditions: The state of the world changes in a way you perceive as negative.
